basic_identification.full_title: Hydrometric Determinations — Flow Measurement in Open Channels Using Structures — Flat-V Weirs (पहला पुनरीक्षण) (First Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Water Resources / Hydrometry (approved by the Water Resources Division Council and finalized by the Hydrometry Sectional Committee, WRD 01, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard specifies standard guidelines, design criteria, and operational procedures for using Flat-V weirs to measure the volumetric flow rate (discharge) of liquids in open channels under steady or slowly varying flow conditions in both modular (free flow) and non-modular (drowned flow) ranges.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Code of Practice / Design and Operational Guidelines (Water Resources Department / Hydrometry)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 13083 is an engineering design and field installation standard rather than a retail consumer product, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product certification stamp. However, compliance with its structural dimensions, cross-slopes, and pressure-tapping positions is strictly mandated in public sector tenders for irrigation channels, river gauging stations, and hydrometric networks (issued by the Central Water Commission, state water resources departments, and municipal water authorities) across India to ensure discharge measurement precision and prevent data disputes.

requirements.detail: The standard Flat-V weir structure must have a triangular profile in the direction of flow, featuring an upstream slope of 1 (vertical) : 2 (horizontal) and a downstream slope of 1 (vertical) : 5 (horizontal) to ensure stable flow separation and high modular limits.

The cross-slope of the crest line shall lie in the range of 0 to 1:10 (shall not be steeper than 1:10). At the limit when the cross-slope is zero, the weir becomes a two-dimensional triangular profile weir.

The upstream head measurement tapping (gauge location) must be positioned at a standard distance of 10H' (where H' is the depth of the V) or as specified to ensure it is outside the local drawdown region.

Provides high modular limits typically ranging from 65 percent to 75 percent. The weir can operate accurately without drowned-flow reduction adjustments even when the downstream tailwater level submerges up to 75 percent of the upstream head.

The weir crest must be kept clean, sharp, and free from clinging debris. If the mean effective radius of the crest exceeds critical limits, refurbishment is required to prevent significant measurement errors at low flows.
The Flat-V weir is approved for gauging purposes in the non-modular (drowned) flow range, provided a pressure-recording tapping is physically incorporated directly at the weir crest.

Any observed or calculated analysis value (including discharge rates, velocity heads, and water stages) used to determine compliance must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960. The number of significant places retained must match the standard's specified value.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 13083 : 2017 (First Revision) is the national Indian Standard code of practice specifying guidelines for measuring liquid flow in open channels using Flat-V weirs. Formulated under the Hydrometry Sectional Committee (WRD 01) and technically aligned with ISO 4377, this standard provides a comprehensive design framework for installing, calibrating, and maintaining Flat-V weirs in river gauging and canal networks. It specifies a standard triangular weir profile (1:2 upstream and 1:5 downstream slopes), details the crest cross-slope limits (up to 1:10), and defines discharge coefficients, head correction factors (such as 0.4 mm to 0.8 mm), and standard uncertainties (1.15% to 1.4%) for different cross-slopes. It also outlines maintenance requirements and allows flow measurements in drowned-flow conditions using a dedicated crest pressure tapping.
